correctness.rationale: The weighted harmonic mean has partials rv²/(rv+su)² and su²/(rv+su)². On strict monotone data the Hermite gradient has nonpositive outer entries and nonnegative inner entries: the latter are bounded below by 1−S−3U=(1−t)³ and S−3V=t³, since the central-secant slope derivatives are less than 3. Translation equivariance gives sum 1, so its maximum norm dual is 1 plus twice the magnitudes of the outer entries. Their derivative bounds are approached simultaneously as the two positive outer secants tend to zero with fixed positive central secant. Taking the directional quotient with (−1,+1,+1,−1) before letting the outer secants vanish realizes this supremum within the strict cone. Segment integration proves the upper bound there; approaching any closed-cone endpoints by adding the same tiny strictly increasing ramp extends by continuity. At t=0,1 the map is a nodal coordinate. For u=q(a,b), v=q(c,b)>0 the derivative of t(1−t)[u(1−t)+vt] is a quadratic with opposite strict signs at 0 and 1 (linear for u=v), hence exactly one interior root. The midpoint lower bound and strict convexity of q in the outer spacing prove unique balancing, attained at t=1/2; direct substitution gives 2 and 14/5. As a→0 with b,c fixed, dividing the profile increment by q(a,b) gives uniform convergence to 2t(1−t)², with maximum 8/27, and q(a,b)∼3b/(2a).
residual_risks: Only the middle cell with standard interior slopes and fixed knots, for two nondecreasing data vectors; not the endpoint slope rules, a relative error bound, or a claim about nonmonotone inputs.

value.rationale: For a standard shape-preserving algorithm, the exact amplification of bounded nodal perturbations is an operationally natural invariant. Dependence on relative position and unequal adjacent spacings matters: the optimal balance under a fixed length budget is unique, while the same monotonicity-preserving rule has unbounded amplification under mesh grading. The sharp coefficient and balance quantify a limitation that range preservation for individual data does not address.
residual_risks: No probabilistic noise or knot-error model, floating-point estimate, or global claim about endpoint-cell sensitivity.
